evidenceAudit.scope: Primary health centre and hospital doctors in Saudi Arabia assessing adults with varicose veins: give information, identify who needs referral to a vascular service (including immediate referral for bleeding), understand what the vascular service does (duplex ultrasound, endothermal ablation, foam sclerotherapy, surgery) and manage varicose veins in pregnancy. Uses NICE CG168, Saudi studies from Riyadh and the polidocanol foam label. Not for the management of venous leg ulcers beyond the referral decision.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-20.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi Ministry of Health or Saudi Health Council varicose vein referral guideline was found; the pathway follows NICE CG168 (2013) and Saudi data are descriptive only.

NICE CG168 is a United Kingdom guideline from 2013; local availability of endothermal ablation, foam sclerotherapy and duplex ultrasound in each Saudi region was not checked, and any 2025 NICE update was not seen.

NICE says to use compression bandaging or hosiery after intervention for no more than 7 days, but the United States label of polidocanol foam says to maintain compression for 2 weeks after treatment; the conflict is flagged for the treating vascular team and the label figure is written only as the label's instruction.

Only one sclerosant (polidocanol injectable foam, a drug and device combination) was written from a label; other sclerosants, the thermal ablation devices and the surgical technique are not described because no verified source for them was read.
Prevalence figures for varicose veins in Saudi Arabia are from clinic-based descriptive studies and cannot be taken as population rates.
The CEAP clinical classification is named from the Saudi studies; its class definitions were not read and are not written.
Figures were read by automated extraction of web, article and label text; spot-check each figure and dose against the source during clinical review.

pathophysiology.summary: Varicose veins are dilated, tortuous veins that cause pain, swelling and skin changes (Riyadh endovenous laser ablation study, Section Introduction). Chronic venous disease affects 20% to 60% of adults worldwide (Arabic CIVIQ-20 study, Section 1). Truncal reflux, backward flow in the great or small saphenous vein, is confirmed by duplex ultrasound and drives treatment (NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.3.1). Complications include deep vein thrombosis, skin changes, leg ulcers, bleeding and thrombophlebitis (NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.1.1). In a Riyadh series of 260 patients treated by laser ablation, 93.1% were women, mostly aged 25 to 45, and 86.2% were CEAP class C2 (Riyadh endovenous laser ablation study, Section Result).

symptoms: Troublesome leg symptoms: pain, aching, discomfort, swelling, heaviness and itching (NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.2.2).
Prominent veins were the most frequent complaint in Riyadh (39.2%), followed by prominent veins with oedema (32.3%) (Riyadh endovenous laser ablation study, Section Result).
Bleeding from a varicose vein (NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.2.1).
physicalSigns: Visible dilated tortuous veins (Riyadh endovenous laser ablation study, Section Introduction).
Lower limb pigmentation or eczema thought to be caused by chronic venous insufficiency (NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.2.2).
Hard, painful superficial veins suggesting superficial vein thrombosis (NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.2.2).
A venous leg ulcer, a break in the skin below the knee not healed within 2 weeks, or a healed ulcer (NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.2.2).
redFlags: Bleeding varicose vein: refer to a vascular service immediately (NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.2.1).
Venous leg ulcer not healed within 2 weeks, or a healed ulcer: refer (NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.2.2).
Superficial vein thrombosis with suspected venous incompetence: refer (NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.2.2).
Acute thromboembolic disease is a contraindication to foam sclerotherapy (Polidocanol foam label, Section Contraindications 4).
precipitants: Female sex and age 25 to 45 years (Riyadh endovenous laser ablation study, Section Result).
Long-standing or heavy physical work, and standing occupations (Riyadh endovenous laser ablation study, Section Result).
Family history, hormonal factors and lifestyle (Riyadh endovenous laser ablation study, Section Introduction).
Obesity and low physical activity (NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.1.1).

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Small cosmetic veins without truncal reflux; referral criteria in NICE depend on symptoms and complications (NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.2.2).

differentials.condition: Chronic venous insufficiency with skin change
differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Pigmentation, eczema or ulcer from venous hypertension (NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.2.2).
Hard, painful vein; may be associated with venous incompetence (NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.2.2).
Swelling and pain of the whole limb; a contraindication to sclerotherapy (Polidocanol foam label, Section Contraindications 4).
Swelling without prominent veins; assess separately (NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.1.1).

clinicalManagement.title: Inform the person
actions: Explain what varicose veins are, their causes, the chance of progression and complications such as deep vein thrombosis, skin changes, leg ulcers, bleeding and thrombophlebitis (NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.1.1).
Advise on weight loss, light to moderate physical activity, avoiding things that worsen symptoms, and when to seek help (NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.1.1).

clinicalManagement.title: Triage for referral
actions: Refer a bleeding varicose vein to a vascular service immediately (NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.2.1).

Refer symptomatic primary or recurrent varicose veins, skin changes from chronic venous insufficiency, superficial vein thrombosis with suspected incompetence, a venous leg ulcer (not healed in 2 weeks) or a healed ulcer (NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.2.2).
Do not offer compression hosiery as treatment unless intervention is unsuitable (NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.3.4).

clinicalManagement.title: Manage bleeding on the way
actions: Treat a bleeding varicose vein as an emergency referral to the vascular service (NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.2.1).

clinicalManagement.title: Assess in the vascular service
actions: Perform duplex ultrasound to confirm varicose veins, map truncal reflux and plan treatment (NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.3.1).

Explain options, benefits and risks, that new veins may develop, that more than one session may be needed, and that recurrence risk is higher after treatment of recurrent veins (NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.1.2).

clinicalManagement.title: Treat truncal reflux
actions: Offer endothermal ablation (radiofrequency or endovenous laser) first (NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.3.2).
If unsuitable, offer ultrasound-guided foam sclerotherapy; if unsuitable, offer surgery (NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.3.2).
Consider treating incompetent tributaries at the same time (NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.3.2).
If compression is used after treatment, do not use it for more than 7 days (NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.3.3).

clinicalManagement.title: Manage varicose veins in pregnancy
actions: Give information on the effect of pregnancy on varicose veins (NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.4.1).
Avoid interventional treatment other than in exceptional circumstances (NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.4.2).
Consider compression hosiery for leg swelling (NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.4.3).

regimens.indication: Treatment of incompetent great saphenous veins, accessory saphenous veins and visible varicosities of the great saphenous system
regimens.patientGroup: Adults with symptomatic superficial venous incompetence
regimens.dose: Up to 5 mL of foam per injection and no more than 15 mL per session; repeat sessions at least 5 days apart if more than 15 mL is needed (Polidocanol foam label, Dosage and Administration 2). Dilution and preparation: none by the clinician; the 180 mg/18 mL canister (10 mg/mL) is activated with the oxygen canister and a transfer unit generates a foam delivering 1% polidocanol; give within 75 seconds of generation and discard if there are visible bubbles (Polidocanol foam label, Dosage and Administration 2 and Description 11).
regimens.route: Intravenous injection under ultrasound guidance through a single cannula into the target trunk vein or by direct injection into varicosities; inject slowly, about 1 mL per second in the great saphenous vein and 0.5 mL per second in accessory veins or varicosities, and confirm venospasm on ultrasound (Polidocanol foam label, Dosage and Administration 2)
regimens.frequency: Single treatment session; repeat only if more than 15 mL is needed (Polidocanol foam label, Dosage and Administration 2)
regimens.duration: Compression bandaging and stockings after treatment: the label says to keep them on for 2 weeks and to walk for at least 10 minutes under observation; NICE limits post-intervention compression to 7 days (Polidocanol foam label, Dosage and Administration 2; NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.3.3)
adjustments: Pregnancy: the label found no drug-associated risk in case reports but notes minimal benefit in treating varicosities during pregnancy, and pregnancy increases thrombosis risk; NICE advises no intervention in pregnancy except in exceptional circumstances (Polidocanol foam label, Section Use in Specific Populations 8.1; NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.4.2).
Children: safety and effectiveness have not been established (Polidocanol foam label, Section Use in Specific Populations 8.4).
Older adults: no important difference in safety or efficacy (Polidocanol foam label, Section Use in Specific Populations 8.5).
Renal and hepatic impairment: no dose adjustment is given in the label read.
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Observe for at least 10 minutes after injection for allergic reaction and anaphylaxis (Polidocanol foam label, Section Warnings and Precautions 5.1).

Watch for signs of venous thrombosis, especially with reduced mobility, previous deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism, recent major surgery or pregnancy (Polidocanol foam label, Section Warnings and Precautions 5.3).
Tissue ischaemia or necrosis if intra-arterial injection or extravasation occurs; consult a vascular surgeon at once (Polidocanol foam label, Section Warnings and Precautions 5.2).
contraindications: Known allergy to polidocanol (Polidocanol foam label, Section Contraindications 4).
Acute thromboembolic disease (Polidocanol foam label, Section Contraindications 4).

branches.entryCriteria: Adult with duplex-confirmed saphenous truncal reflux for whom endothermal ablation is unsuitable, with no acute thromboembolic disease, no polidocanol allergy and no marked arterial disease.

medicationPlan.note: Most patients are referred and treated by a vascular service; the only medicine written is polidocanol injectable foam, the second option in the NICE treatment order when endothermal ablation is unsuitable (NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.3.2). It is a drug and device combination used only by trained clinicians with ultrasound. The United States label's 2-week compression advice differs from NICE's limit of 7 days (see unverified). SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: A bleeding varicose vein (NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.2.1).

diagnosticCriteria.criterion: Routine referral to a vascular service
diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Symptomatic primary or recurrent varicose veins; skin changes from chronic venous insufficiency; superficial vein thrombosis with suspected incompetence; venous leg ulcer or healed ulcer (NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.2.2).
Duplex ultrasound to confirm varicose veins and extent of truncal reflux (NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.3.1).
Endothermal ablation first; foam sclerotherapy if unsuitable; surgery if foam is unsuitable (NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.3.2).
Do not offer to treat varicose veins unless intervention is unsuitable; after intervention use for no more than 7 days (NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.3.3 and 1.3.4).
No intervention in pregnancy other than in exceptional circumstances; consider compression hosiery for swelling (NICE CG168, Recommendation 1.4.2 and 1.4.3).

teaching.scope: Primary health centre and hospital doctors in Saudi Arabia assessing adults with varicose veins: give information, identify who needs referral to a vascular service (including immediate referral for bleeding), understand what the vascular service does (duplex ultrasound, endothermal ablation, foam sclerotherapy, surgery) and manage varicose veins in pregnancy. Uses NICE CG168, Saudi studies from Riyadh and the polidocanol foam label. Not for the management of venous leg ulcers beyond the referral decision.
learningObjectives: Refer symptomatic veins, skin changes, thrombosis and ulcers.
Duplex ultrasound confirms and plans treatment.
Endothermal ablation first, then foam, then surgery.
pitfalls: Delaying referral of a bleeding vein.
Ordering duplex scanning in primary care without referral when the pathway sends it to the vascular service.
keyPoints: Do not use compression stockings as a substitute for referral.
Do not treat varicose veins surgically in pregnancy except in exceptional circumstances.
Foam sclerotherapy is contraindicated in acute thromboembolic disease.

patientEducation: Varicose veins are usually not dangerous, but they can cause aching, swelling, skin changes and ulcers.
If a vein bleeds, lie down, raise the leg, press firmly with a clean cloth and get urgent help.
Light to moderate exercise and weight loss help your symptoms.
Treatment is done by a vascular team; new veins may appear and you may need more than one session.
After treatment, keep walking and follow the bandage and stocking advice you are given.
lifestyleAndDiet: Walk regularly and avoid standing still for long periods.
Tell your doctor about any skin change or sore on your leg.
mdtReferrals: Primary care doctor and nurse; vascular surgeon; vascular technologist for duplex ultrasound; interventional radiologist; wound care nurse; obstetrician for pregnancy.
dischargeCriteria: Discharge after treatment when the treated vein is checked, compression advice and activity advice are given, and warning signs of thrombosis and allergy are explained.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Duplex follow-up per the treating vascular team; return for new symptoms, ulcers, or signs of venous thrombosis.
